testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

survived.claim: kindHolder(live, "run", n) matches only REVIEWER-shaped runner names, so an open `review=wf:<runId>` launch of PR N, which liveOnLedger does report as live under its runId, does not protect it: the root sweep evicts the installed paths of every tree in that live review's run-* root. The receipt reason then says "with no open review launch of PR #N on the ledger", which is false.
survived.evidence: PROBE in copy/tests/reclaim-scratch.test.mjs: f.ledger(["#6 impl-6=PR#7 → PR#7 · review=wf:abc123"], …); f.states({7: OPEN}); prDirectory(f); run --root --apply → `PROBE-EVICTED [... "/pr7/run-ddddddd1/correctness/copy","/pr7/run-ddddddd1/snapshot-abc1234","/pr7/run-ddddddd1/verify-correctness/finding-1/copy"]`, `PROBE-INSTALLED /pr7/run-ddddddd1/snapshot-abc1234 false` (all three run trees lost node_modules). `node -e` liveOnLedger(same row).tokens → `[{"name":"abc123","token":"review=wf:abc123","row":"#6"}]`, kindHolder(["impl-6","abc123"],"run",7) → `undefined`. wf launches are still accepted grammar and documented as live (fleet-event.mjs:107-110 `review-failed` takes `wf:<runId>`; phase-0.md:611,628; SKILL.md:808 retries a failed `review-pr` workflow).
survived.suggested_fix: Decide 'run' liveness from the open launches themselves rather than from the name: for each live token whose `token` matches REVIEW, bind it to the PR of the row it sits on (`row`/streamId), so a wf:<runId> launch on PR N's row holds PR N's run-* trees. Add the wf case to the '(12) an open review launch of PR <N> keeps the run-* trees' test.

survived.claim: Any repository whose pinned tree holds a submodule gitlink or an `export-ignore` attribute can never get a measuring copy: `git archive` drops those entries, the copy's tree differs from the pin's, and the script exits 1 `tree-mismatch` every time — while every prompt this PR changes forbids making a copy by hand, so every refuter run in such a repo is inconclusive and every in-scope suggestion defers.
survived.evidence: PROBE (copy/tests/measure-copy.test.mjs): `.gitattributes` = `tracked.txt export-ignore` → `PROBE-EI 1 tree-mismatch the copy's tree b59dbd… is not the tree 7c2a70… of 4c33e9…`; a 160000 gitlink `vendor/sub` + .gitmodules → `PROBE-SUB 1 tree-mismatch the copy's tree 578faa… is not the tree 93ecb8… of 649ed3…`.
survived.suggested_fix: Materialise the pin without archive attributes, e.g. `git -C <worktree> --work-tree=<dest> checkout <pin> -- .` into the new repo or `git read-tree`+`checkout-index` against a temporary index, and decide explicitly how gitlinks are recorded (e.g. `git update-index --cacheinfo 160000,…`) so the tree check compares like with like; at minimum name the cause in the tree-mismatch message.

votes.reason: I reproduced the mismatch on the snapshot's measure-copy.mjs. The fixture was a repo with `.gitattributes` = `t.txt export-ignore`, pinned at a committed SHA. Run: `node measure-copy.mjs --worktree r --pin 6fa8ac… --dest pr1/run-x/d --pr 1 --scratch B` → exit 1, kind `tree-mismatch` ('the copy's tree 7d1456… is not the tree ef3d0d… of 6fa8ac…'). The code path at line ~195 confirms this: the copy is built with `git archive | tar -x`, then `git add -A -f`, and its tree is compared with the pin's tree. `export-ignore` entries (and gitlinks) are dropped by `git archive`, so the trees differ every time. I did not read the prompt text for the 'no hand-made copy' part, so the downstream consequence of every refuter run being inconclusive is taken from the claim. I did not run a gitlink fixture; the export-ignore case alone shows the script's behavior. survived.claim: kindHolder(live, "run", n) matches only runner names of the form review-pr-<n>[-x]. An open `review=wf:<runId>` launch is live under its runId, so it holds no run-* root. The root sweep therefore evicts the installed trees of a PR whose review is still running, and the receipt reason says "no open review launch of PR #7 on the ledger", which is false.
survived.evidence: liveOnLedger(["7 PR#7 review=wf:wfrun123","8 PR#8 review=member:review-pr-8"],[]) gives names ["wfrun123","review-pr-8"], and kindHolder(names,"run",7) is undefined while kindHolder(names,"run",8) is review-pr-8. End to end, I appended a case to a copy of tests/reclaim-scratch.test.mjs with ledger row `#6 impl-6=PR#7 → PR#7 · review=wf:wfrun123` and PR 7 OPEN, then ran `reclaim-scratch.mjs --root <root> --apply`. It exited 0 and all three run-root trees printed EVICTED (node_modules gone). The receipt reasons were "a tree in a review run root, with no open review launch of PR #7 on the ledger". The existing test with `review=member:review-pr-7` keeps the trees.
survived.suggested_fix: Resolve which PR an open wf launch belongs to, for example from the launch's token stream or row (liveOnLedger already knows the row key), and treat it as a run-root holder for that PR. At minimum, treat any open `review=wf:` launch on that PR's stream as holding its run-* roots. The existing prHolder() has the same gap and could share the fix.

survived.claim: `sh -c 'git archive … | tar -x …'` has no pipefail, so a failing `git archive` exits 0 through tar. The `archive-failed` kind and git's stderr never surface for that failure. It is reported as `tree-mismatch` against an empty-tree copy, which mislabels the cause.
survived.evidence: `sh -c 'git -C "$1" archive "$2" | tar -x -C "$3"' sh wt deadbeef… out` printed `fatal: not a tree object` and then status=0. With a PATH shim whose git exits 128 on `archive`, measure-copy.mjs exited 1 with kind "tree-mismatch" and message "the copy's tree 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 is not the tree 0d8a47… of d16fb13e…" (4b825dc… is the empty tree). The git error text is dropped. The script still refuses, so this is a mislabel, not a false success.
survived.suggested_fix: Run `git archive` as its own spawnSync, check its status and stderr, then feed its stdout to `tar -x` through `input`. Or use `set -o pipefail` where the shell supports it, or write the archive to a temp file and extract from that.

Line 196 only reports `archive-failed` when sh's status is non-zero, so that kind never fires for a git failure. The empty extraction falls through to init/commit and then to the `tree-mismatch` check at line ~216. I did not run the PATH-shim end-to-end case. The code path is clear from reading it.
